content.heading: Vicarious liability
content.text: An employer is vicariously liable for a tort committed by a servant in the course of employment. The claimant must establish the servant's tort and the employment relationship. An act is in the course of employment if it is a wrongful mode of doing something the servant was authorised to do, or is otherwise so closely connected with the employment that it is fair to treat the employer as responsible. An employer is not generally liable for the torts of a true independent contractor, save where a non-delegable duty or other exception applies. Vicarious liability is distinct from the employer's own negligence.
